title: Linear Seating Arrangement: Rows, Facing, and Fixed Seats

questions.question: A person faces north. As seen on the page, their LEFT hand points which way?
options: To the top of the page
To your left (west)
To your right (east)
It depends on the seat number
questions.rationale: With north up on the page, a north-facing person's left matches your left — toward the west. Only a south-facing person's left flips to your right.

questions.question: In a row facing south, the clue 'S sits immediately to the left of R' places S in which direction from R on the page?
options: One seat to the page's left of R
One seat to the page's right of R
Two seats to the page's left of R
Directly opposite R
questions.rationale: A south-facing person's left is the page's right, so 'immediately to the left of R' means the adjacent seat on the page's right of R — the facing convention flips the clue.

questions.question: Which clue type should you place FIRST when solving a linear arrangement?
options: Negative clues such as 'F is not at any end'
Definite clues such as 'G is 3rd from the left'
Count-equality clues
The longest clue in the list
questions.rationale: Definite clues fix positions outright and create the anchors; relative clues chain onto them, and negative or count-based clues are used last to break ties.

questions.question: In the worked seven-person row (D, B, G, A, F, E, C from left), who sits exactly in the middle seat?
options: G
A
F
E
questions.rationale: With seats 1 to 7 occupied by D, B, G, A, F, E, C, the middle seat 4 is A, who was placed by clue 3 as immediately to the right of G.

questions.question: In that same row, who are F's immediate neighbours?
options: G and A
A and E
B and E
E and C
questions.rationale: F occupies seat 5, between A in seat 4 and E in seat 6, so F's neighbours are A and E.

questions.question: In the two-row example, Row 1 faces south and Row 2 faces north. What does the clue 'E sits at the right end of Row 2' mean on the page?
options: E is at the page's left of Row 2
E is at the page's right of Row 2
E is in the middle of Row 2
E is opposite the middle of Row 1
questions.rationale: Row 2 faces north, so the sitters' right matches the page's right: E takes the rightmost seat of Row 2, seat 5.

questions.question: In a facing-variable question, a clue says 'D sits to the left of C' where C faces north. Where is D relative to C on the page?
options: Somewhere to the page's left of C
Somewhere to the page's right of C
Always immediately beside C
The clue is unusable
questions.rationale: Directional clues are read in the frame of the person being referenced. C faces north, and a north-facing person's left is the page's left, so D lies to the page's left of C — regardless of which way D personally faces.

questions.question: What is bracket notation used for in linear seating?
options: Marking which clues have been checked twice
Writing linked pairs as blocks that slide along the seats
Recording the facing direction of each row
Numbering the seats from the left
questions.rationale: Bracket notation fixes linked people, such as [A G] for an immediate pair, so the whole block can be slid along the blanks until other clues lock it in place.

questions.question: A clue reads 'A is at one of the extreme ends.' What should you do?
options: Guess one end and continue
Ignore the clue as too vague
Carry both branches until another clue kills one
Place A in the middle temporarily
questions.rationale: The clue creates two possible branches. Keep both arrangements alive and let a later clue — often a negative one — eliminate one branch.

questions.question: What is the mandatory final step after completing any seating diagram?
options: Re-check the arrangement against every clue, one by one
Count the people again
Draw the diagram a second time from memory
Convert all relative clues to negative clues
questions.rationale: One early wrong branch silently poisons the rest of the diagram, so verify the finished arrangement against every clue before answering questions.
